text:
sneha: heads-up, canary run for raven-lite-int4 shows funcall parse_fail_rate jump from 1.1% -> 11.8% after the quant bundle landed. stack traces point to JSON decode errors on tool output.

david: ouch. any concrete examples? happy to repro locally.

sneha: past 30m samples attached in traces. common pattern: valid json body then 1-2 trailing control chars (\u0007 / \u0000) before newline, decoder chokes in strict parser. sample: ```{"action": "open_file", "path": "/tmp/x"}\u0007\n```

amy: seen similar with recent kv-cache prefixing in int4 canary. thought we trimmed padding bytes but maybe quant kernel emits nonprintable tail. :eyes:

ken: canary-bot shows these are concentrated on shorter outputs (<120 tokens) and when batching=1. when batch>1 the decoder sees trailing junk in 12% of failing requests.

lina: quick telemetry: query -> `parse_fail_rate by model, quant, seq_len` returned: raven-lite-int4: 11.8% (seq_len <120), raven-fp16: 0.9%. i've uploaded 12 sample payloads to /s3/canary/traces/1712003333/ with raw bytes.

marta: for triage: 1) reproduce with local int4 runner and same tokenizer 2) instrument kernel output to dump last 32 bytes 3) run a strict-json sanitizer pre-parse that strips trailing control chars and record how many pass.

canary-bot: deploy raven-lite-int4-canary @ 1712002000 -> hostset a,b,c. 36 successes / 6 failures in last 15m. latest failure_id=cnry-1712003302.

david: i can repro off the sample. quick fix idea: avoid strict JSON parse at first stage — try NDJSON tolerant parse that ignores trailing control chars and then full schema validation on cleaned payload. would mask the root cause though.

ken: agreed, but we have to be careful not to silently accept malformed funcalls. customer contracts expect exact exec. i'd prefer a two-step: 1) strict parse -> on error run sanitized parse and emit telemetry (sanitized=true) 2) increment retry budget if sanitized parse succeeded.

amy: small regex that removes trailing C0 control bytes: `s/[\x00-\x1F]+$//` (applied only if strict parse fails). put into call-rescue layer.

lina: telemetry after applying sanitize in a local canary: sanitize success rate 9/10 of prior failures. but we still saw 2 reproductions where the payload had an interspersed \u0000 in the middle of string, broke heuristics.

marta: for long term: 1) run kernel output byte-sanity test in CI (random seeds + short outputs) 2) add a sanitizer opt-in flag on canary routes 3) add kernel-level fix with quant team to ensure no trailing pad bytes are written to stream.

sneha: action items — david and amy to push a rescue-layer PR with telemetry tag `rescue=sanitize_controlchars` (target EOD), ken to add retry-budget increment logic and alert if sanitized parse >5% for 1h, marta to own kernel CI test and coordinate with quant team. i'll run a 6h soft-canary with sanitize opt-in and report.

ken: also add a quick eval: compare funcall correctness on sanitized vs non-sanitized outputs against our golden set to ensure we don't mask truncations.

david: PR draft soon. adding sample reproducer and small harness patch that feeds raw bytes into both strict and tolerant parsers.

amy: nice. if we get an immediate reduction in user-facing errors we can keep sanitize as a temporary mitigation while kernel fix lands.

sneha: thanks all — ping me for access to the sample bucket. i'll update the canary dashboard with a separate series for `sanitized_parse_rate`. :thumbsup:
